newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIANS DOMINATE DOWNHILL TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIANS DOMINATE DOWNHILL TRAINING.

text.p: Werner Franz led the way on Thursday as the dominant Austrians clocked the four fastest times in final training for two men's World Cup downhills in Italy on Friday and Saturday.

On a grey day in Val Gardena, visibility on the 3.4 km Saslong piste was not as good as it had been on Wednesday and the times were more than a second slower although low temperatures made the snow slightly faster.
Franz, second in the opening men's downhill of the season at Val d'Isere on Sunday, clocked two minutes 01.31 seconds ahead of Josef Strobl, Hannes Trinkl and Fritz Strobl.
It was a familiar tale after the Austrians took the top six places in training in Val d'Isere, the top four in the race and two of the top three spots in Wednesday's training here.
The two unrelated Strobls later posed together near the finish area. "He has the same name as me and of course you can be very fast with this name," said Josef.
Italy's Kristian Ghedina was fifth fastest. "They are all colossal," the bearded Italian said afterwards.
His words contributed to a growing sense of awe around the Austrian team.
"They've said that I'm built like a wardrobe? Yes, it's true but it's all due to Wiener Schnitzel," Fritz Strobl was quoted as saying by one Italian newspaper on Thursday.
Ghedina attributed it more to sausage and potatoes than the popular breaded veal escalopes credited by Strobl.
Canada's Rob Boyd, twice a winner here in the 1980s, was seventh fastest but almost a second slower than Franz.
"The icy turns are a bit icier than yesterday and you really have to be good on the outside ski, really stand on it," he advised his team mates by walkie-talkie at the finish.
"Through the Ciaslat (turn) the light is a little bit flat...the snow's a few seconds slower but you'd never know it."
France's Luc Alphand, World Cup downhill champion for the past two seasons, was ninth fastest but not attributing too much importance to what was only a training run.
"I got a pretty good feeling," he said. "Today I was not trying to be fast but to enjoy it. I had an exciting run."
Like several skiers, he took time to send a happy birthday message to Alberto Tomba, who turned 30 on Thursday.
"Happy Birthday Alberto," the 31-year-old beamed. "I know what it's like to be 30 so good luck to you."
